newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia YTL in Zimbabwe power project.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia YTL in Zimbabwe power project.

text.p: Malaysian independent power producer YTL Corp Bhd plans to invest 1.5 billion ringgit in the privatisation of Zimbabwe's electricity generation systems, the national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.
YTL signed a letter of intent for the project with the Zimbabwean government on Sunday, the news agency said.
YTL owns a 51 percent stake in Africa Power Ltd, which has been entrusted with the privatisation project by the Zimbabwean government.
Francis Yeoh, managing director of YTL, was quoted as saying that the project would be the company's largest overseas investment to date.
Officials from YTL were unavailable for further comment.
The project will involve the privatisation of the Hwange Power Station in northern Zimbabwe. Subsequently, its six power generators will be leased to Africa Power.
Africa Power will then add two more power stations to the complex, thereby increasing the current capacity of 920 megawatts to 1,590 megawatts
The project is expected to be financed via a combination of equity and project financing, Bernama said.
Yeoh was quoted as saying that he expected Zimbabwe to become a net exporter of power in the future. It is currently a net importer of power.
YTL was the first independent power producer in Malaysia. The company's first power plant, located in Paka in the northern Malaysian state of Terengganu, came on line in September 1995.
